title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint: Persistent high blood sugar.

HPI: The patient is a known patient with type 1 diabetes who presents today for a follow-up evaluation. The patient reports that their blood glucose levels have been poorly controlled over the last two weeks. They note frequent episodes of hyperglycemia despite adherence to their current regimen. The patient has been using insulin long-term and reports no changes to their routine. They deny any acute illnesses or recent infections that might contribute to the elevated readings.

Medication List: Insulin (long-term).

Exam: The patient appears in no acute distress. Physical examination reveals a stable gait and normal neurological function. Skin is intact without signs of infection. Vital signs are within normal limits.

Assessment: The patient has type 1 diabetes mellitus complicated by hyperglycemia. The current management strategy appears insufficient to maintain target glucose ranges.

Plan: We will adjust the insulin dosage to better manage the hyperglycemia. The patient will monitor blood glucose more frequently and keep a detailed log for review at the next appointment. Follow-up in two weeks.
explanations: Type 1 diabetes with hyperglycemia / poor control: E10.65.
Do not assign Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes; insulin use is inherent.

distractors.why: Z79.4 is not assigned for type 1 diabetes.
